lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- Twelve Point Five
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fábia | Lesson 9 -- Twelve Point Five

listenings.text: Right, the quarter. Revenue was one point four eight million. Margin, twenty-two percent. Overhead, four hundred and twelve thousand. Headcount cost, two hundred and sixty-eight thousand. That is the quarter. Any questions?

Now the same four lines, with a comparison in each one. Revenue closed at one point four eight million. That is nine percent higher than last quarter. The margin is twenty-two percent. That is three points lower than last year. Overhead is up twelve and a half percent. It is the highest since twenty twenty-three. Two thirds of that is the new warehouse.

matching.title: Match the word to its meaning
defs: all the money a business takes in, before costs
what is left after you take the costs away
what you expect the numbers to be, before they happen
the difference between the plan and what really happened
the standard number you compare yourself against
the cost of running the business, whatever you sell

items.situation: Revenue is 1,480,000. Last quarter, 1,360,000. One sentence.
tips: Revenue is one point four eight million, higher than last quarter.

items.situation: Margin is 22% now, 25% a year ago. One sentence.
tips: The margin is twenty-two percent, three points lower than last year.

items.situation: Overhead is the biggest in three years. One sentence.
tips: Overhead is the highest it has been since 2023.
up twelve and a half percent

items.situation: You expected 1,400,000 and closed at 1,480,000. One sentence.
tips: We are ahead of forecast by about eighty thousand.

items.situation: The client asks: "Is twelve days good?" One sentence.
tips: The benchmark is fourteen days, so we are slightly better.

items.situation: Close the report. One sentence: which line to watch.
tips: The line to watch is the warehouse, not the margin.
because two thirds of it is ...

arguebank.label: Useful language
items: B has more information and less meaning.
Twenty numbers with nothing to compare them with.
In A I know where to look in ten seconds.
A figure on its own is not analysis.
The client is paying for the comparison, not the ledger.
B is what a system prints. A is what a person says.
There is one client for whom B works: ...
What is missing from B is ...
A tells me the line to watch.
